judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward definitional paragraph; the only soft spot is that it identifies the Lender by name without making clear whether 'Lender' is a party to or merely a subject of the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The arbitration section expressly re-defines 'we' and 'us' to include officers, agents and affiliates and gives 'Lender' rights to elect arbitration and waive jury trial (c017, c018, c009), which does not sit easily with this clause's narrower definition of the contracting parties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains a comma splice ('We do not promise that you will actually receive a loan, All credit decisions...') and vague service commitments ('where available', 'may be provided throughout the term', 'estimated period ... one day'), plus a seven-item list of services whose enforceability boundary is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The statement that 'we are not a lender or fiduciary' and that the LOC 'secures your repayment of the loan on its due date' must be read with the LOC clause (c006) and the Default clause (c007); the fit is workable, though the 'one day' service period sits awkwardly against fees earned over the whole term in c004.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, definite sentence asserting that the CAB fee is not interest but is disclosed as a finance charge; the characterisation could be contested, but nothing in the wording is ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the Cost and Payment Terms clause (c004), which likewise separates the Lender's 10% interest from the CAB fee inside the Finance Charge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Every material economic term is a blank ('$___', '°%', 'ofS', 'Joan'), and the rebate promise is doubly vague — the fee is 'earned in advance at the inception' yet subject to a 'partial rebate' and a 'refund of part of the CAB fee based on a prorated daily basis for the final period'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The blanks are irreconcilable with the signature block's certification that the customer received 'THIS CREDIT SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH ALL NECESSARY SPACES COMPLETED' (c029), and the 'earned in advance' language sits against the cancellation refund promise in c032.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The charges are quantified and the '$30 or the State Allowed Returned Item Fee, whichever is greater' formula is definite; 'attorneys' fees, and costs of collection' is open-ended but unremarkable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It divides charges between CAB and Lender consistently with c004 and c006, and the attorneys'-fee entitlement is repeated in the Collection Expenses clause (c012) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing sentences are visibly corrupted and truncated ('If an unlgyuful excess occurs', 'reduced to the maximug peepee law', 'we may calculate charges by amortiz'), leaving an operative savings sentence that does not finish; the LOC is also called 'irrevocable' yet 'automatically revoked' on cancellation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The truncated savings language duplicates the COMPLIANCE clause (c010), which supplies the missing words, and the automatic revocation on cancellation must be read with the cancellation notices (c030–c033); the overlap is largely harmonisable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The remedy list ends in an unbounded catch-all ('any other right or remedy allowed by law'), and the phrase 'seek collection of any check or similar security you have provided us' is genuinely ambiguous as to what collection methods it authorises.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against the Collection Expenses clause (c012), which forbids threatening or pursuing criminal charges over a check given as security, the two provisions pull in opposite directions on whether a check can be pressed through criminal process — the central fight in this litigation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dense string of waivers qualified twice by 'to the extent permitted by law', and the reservation that 'we are not required to file suit or arbitrate' is opaque in a contract that elsewhere makes arbitration the exclusive route.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly rubs against the arbitration agreement (c016: 'You and we agree to arbitrate Claims instead of having them decided in court') and c023 ('all Claims must be arbitrated'), because here the seller reserves the right to 'sue or arbitrate' at its option.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause turns on whether the customer has 'reject[ed]' the Arbitration Agreement, a term used nowhere else, and it purports to bind 'Lender' as a waiving party without Lender signing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The arbitration section speaks of 'opt[ing] out' within 30 days (c021), not 'rejecting', and c022 separately disclaims jury trial only if arbitration is chosen, so the three jury-related provisions must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional usury savings clause; the reduction to 'the maximum lawful rate or amount' is a determinate standard and the OCR slip ('applicable Jaw') does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the savings language embedded in c006 and is consistent with the severability provisions in c024 and c028.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A reasonable opportunity of not less than 60 days to cure the claim' and 'Any corrective action shall relieve us and Lender of any liability' are both indeterminate and drafted wholly for the drafter's benefit, inviting construction against it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conditions 'initiating any claim' that the agreement is unenforceable on 60 days' notice, while the arbitration agreement makes 'the validity of this arbitration agreement' an arbitrable Claim that either side may elect 'at any time' (c017, c018), leaving the sequence of the two gates unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The criminal-charges sentence closes an enumerated list with a general catch-all ('forgery, fraud, theft, or other criminal conduct') whose reach is precisely the kind of ejusdem generis question courts construe, and it shifts from 'you' to 'the consumer' and from the parties to an impersonal 'A person', obscuring whom it binds.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is in evident tension with the Default clause's right to 'seek collection of any check or similar security you have provided us' (c007) and with the customer's warranty in c029(e) that the check account is 'legitimate, open, and active', which is the predicate of a worthless-check complaint.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One short, definite stipulation; 'for all purposes' is broad but there is nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports the FAA choice in c025 and the arbitration agreement generally, with no competing provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain and one-sided but definite: the seller may transfer 'at our discretion', the customer may not without consent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses assignment; a transferee's ability to invoke the arbitration agreement (c017's extension of 'we/us' to affiliates) is the only loose end.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely informational address and telephone details with no operative content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The addresses differ from the notice addresses in c011, c021 and c033 (which name 'PLS Financial Services' and a 'CAB Cancellation' attention line), but nothing turns on the difference here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'You and we agree to arbitrate Claims instead of having them decided in court' is stated as an unconditional agreement, yet the operative machinery that follows is election-based, creating the mandatory/permissive ambiguity that courts routinely construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It omits Lender, whom c018 and c022 treat as an electing party, and it conflicts with c008's reservation that 'we are not required to file suit or arbitrate' and with the opt-out right in c021.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is extraordinarily broad — '(d) the actions of you, us, Lender, or third parties' — and its carve-outs ('an action that you elect to bring in small claims court or equivalent court') leave the outer boundary of what must be arbitrated genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reaches claims under 'any prior credit services agreement', which does not sit comfortably with c021's statement that 'Only those disputes ... arising under this Agreement will be excluded from arbitration', and its breadth collides with c008's reservation of a right to sue.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Either you, we, or Lender may give written notice ... at any time, even if the other party has begun a lawsuit' invites argument about how far a party may litigate before electing, and 'any other arbitrator ... reasonably satisfactory to us' is an indeterminate, one-sided standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The at-any-time election is hard to reconcile with c008's reservation that the seller 'is not required to ... arbitrate' and with c016's flat statement that the parties agree to arbitrate rather than litigate; the judgment-entered cut-off also interacts with c011's pre-suit notice gate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The venue options end in 'or such other location as we or Lender may agree', which omits the customer's agreement and is ambiguous about whose consent is needed; there is also a comma splice ('rules of civil procedure or evidence, Unless').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the FAA choice in c025 and the fee-advance provisions above it, with no competing venue or procedure clause elsewhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, mechanical confirmation clause; the deeming of the place of decision is artificial but determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c019's hearing-location rules and c025's FAA governing law; nothing else addresses entry of judgment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opt-out notice must be sent to 'PLS Financial Services', an entity different from the contracting 'PLS Loan Store of Texas, Inc.', and the sentence 'Only those disputes ... arising under this Agreement will be excluded from arbitration' is opaque about the effect of an opt-out on related transactions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts with the Definition of Claim (c017), which sweeps in prior agreements and the actions of third parties, and with c009's reference to 'reject[ing]' the arbitration agreement, so the scope and vocabulary of opting out are not uniform across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain explanatory language about the consequences of arbitration; 'neither you nor we' omits Lender, but the sentence is otherwise definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the separate jury waiver in c009, which operates in litigation and disclaims any effect on the arbitration agreement, so the two jury provisions must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Emphatic and repetitive but definite; the only friction is that the waiver is expressed as conditional ('If either you, we, or Lender ... choose arbitration') while the sentences that follow state an unconditional prohibition on class procedure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The conditional opening sits against c016's unconditional agreement to arbitrate and against the opt-out right in c021, but the severability sentence in c024 largely absorbs the strain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard severability and conflict-precedence sentence, definite in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the general severability/reformation clause in c028, which requires reformation 'if practicable' rather than mere excision, so two different severance regimes apply to the arbitration text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Governed by ... the Federal Arbitration Act' as an exception to Texas law is imprecise, since the FAA supplies no rules of contract formation or unconscionability, leaving the applicable law for those questions unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with c019 ('This arbitration agreement shall be governed by the Federal Arbitration Act') and c013's interstate-commerce stipulation; the residual role of Texas law in deciding whether an arbitration agreement was formed is the live gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A cautionary statutory-style notice with no operative obligations; its content is advisory rather than construable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its warning that the product meets only 'immediate short-term cash needs' points differently from the instalment structure and refinancing machinery in c002 and c004, a mild recital-versus-operative tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure regulatory contact information with no operative effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside, and does not conflict with, the pre-suit notice requirement in c011 or the arbitration agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The entire agreement between you and us relating to the subject matter of this Agreement' is circular, and 'reformed if practicable so as to achieve its intended purpose(s)' is an indeterminate savings standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The merger claim is difficult to square with the separate Credit Services Disclosure Statement, the loan agreement with the Lender and the two Notices of Cancellation that c029 and c030 treat as part of the transaction, and its reformation rule differs from the arbitration severability rule in c024.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A string of acknowledgments and warranties in one sentence, including the vague warranty that the customer has 'no intention to file a petition' in bankruptcy and that the account is 'legitimate, open, and active'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The certification that the form was received 'WITH ALL NECESSARY SPACES COMPLETED' cannot be reconciled with the wholly blank economic terms in c004, and the account warranty in (e) sits against c012's bar on pursuing criminal charges over a security check.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'BEFORE MIDNIGHT OF THE THIRD DAY AFTER THE DATE OF THE TRANSACTION' fixes the deadline by reference to 'the transaction', a term the Agreement never defines.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts with the attached Notices of Cancellation (c031), which measure the same right as 'within three days after the date the contract is signed', so two different triggers and two different formulations govern one cancellation right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Within three days after the date the contract is signed' is a clear enough period on its own, though it does not say whether the third day itself counts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states the deadline differently from the operative NOTICE in c030 ('before midnight of the third day after the date of the transaction'), an inconsistency in the same instrument about when the cancellation right lapses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite promise to return 'any payment made by you under this contract' within 10 days of receipt of the cancellation notice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against c004's statement that the CAB fee 'is earned in advance at the inception of the loan' and against c006's automatic revocation of the LOC, leaving the interaction of cancellation, earned fees and the Lender's loan unresolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deadline is left blank ('not later than midnight on') and the seller's address is stated twice in a single garbled run-on, so the operative cut-off date is missing from the form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The blank date is at odds with c029's certification that all necessary spaces were completed and with the fixed three-day periods stated in c030 and c031.
